SWP-001.title: Foundations of Child Protection
SWP-001.outcome: Recognise protection concerns, respond safely, and follow the local reporting pathway.

modules.title: Child protection foundations
modules.focus: child rights, safeguarding principles, roles, and the distinction between concern, risk, and harm

modules.title: Recognising and responding
modules.focus: indicators of abuse/neglect, trauma-informed communication, documentation, immediate safety, and boundaries

modules.title: Reporting and case coordination
modules.focus: mandated reporting, referral pathways, confidentiality limits, multi-agency coordination, and reflective case scenario

SWP-002.title: Family Preservation & Kinship Care
SWP-002.outcome: Plan safe, strengths-based support that preserves family relationships whenever appropriate.

modules.title: Family-centred assessment
modules.focus: strengths, risks, culture, family networks, and child voice

modules.title: Preservation and safety planning
modules.focus: in-home services, measurable safety plans, crisis support, and review points

modules.title: Kinship care practice
modules.focus: identifying kin, caregiver assessment, support needs, contact planning, and permanency review

SWP-003.title: Permanency Planning & Reunification
SWP-003.outcome: Develop timely, child-centred permanency plans and assess reunification readiness.

modules.title: Permanency principles
modules.focus: stability, attachment, timelines, child participation, and concurrent planning

modules.title: Reunification practice
modules.focus: readiness indicators, parent support, supervised contact, risk reassessment, and transition planning

modules.title: Alternative permanency
modules.focus: guardianship, adoption, long-term care, cultural continuity, and case review

items.prompt: A fictional family plan treats poverty alone as proof that a child must leave home. A possible kinship caregiver has not been assessed; reunification is promised after one meeting. Give five corrections within an introductory learner role.
items.model_answer: Distinguish concerns, risks and actual safety needs; consider family strengths, support and a reviewed safety plan; assess kinship suitability and support; consider child views, contact and context; and treat reunification/permanency as reviewed decisions for authorised practitioners, not promises or learner determinations.

items.prompt: In a fictional planning meeting an adult answers for a child who communicates differently. A vote is described as consent and no one explains what can change. Give five improvements.
items.model_answer: Clarify decision influence; offer appropriate communication support and alternatives without assuming inability; support a voluntary view without forced disclosure; explain realistic information boundaries without inferring consent from a vote or silence; and record how views were considered with an accessible response and review route. Voice alone does not prove safety or transfer adult responsibility.

items.prompt: A fictional organisation relies on a policy poster and one screening certificate. A volunteer handles a complaint about their own conduct; partners have no reporting arrangements. Give five corrections.
items.model_answer: Connect policy to assigned operational responsibilities; use contextual safer recruitment, conduct, induction and supervision without treating one check as a guarantee; provide accessible bounded reporting and qualified safeguarding routes; address conflicts through an authorised impartial response rather than learner investigation; and review partner responsibilities, implementation and follow-up. Low report counts do not prove safety.

items.prompt: Develop a conditional review plan across all eight CPS courses for a fictional family-support programme in a displacement setting. Material hardship is treated as grounds for separation; kinship support is unassessed; reunification is promised; communication needs are overlooked; partner data are shared openly; volunteer supervision and reporting routes are unclear; and a caregiver-support abstract is treated as a delivery manual. Explain priorities, responsibilities, evidence, review and introductory-learning limits.
items.model_answer: Integrate concern recognition and immediate safety boundaries; family strengths, support and reviewed safety planning; assessed kinship and evidence-informed permanency; supported voluntary child voice with honest influence and feedback; necessary controlled information and accountable referral; safer organisational people, reporting, partners and supervision; outcome-specific research interpretation without blame or unauthorised treatment; and coordinated inclusive emergency services with separation safeguards. Set conditional owners, unresolved approvals and review points. Do not recruit children, investigate, disclose real records, promise placement or claim deployment competence.

items.prompt: Critique a fictional claim of proven child safety based on a policy poster, fewer complaints, attendance, caregiver self-reports and a participation vote. The programme offers instant reunification, calls a public case spreadsheet transparent, and promises certification after reading slides. Use all eight CPS domains to propose corrections and identify missing evidence and authority.
items.model_answer: Separate concern recognition from proof of safety, family support from automatic separation, and assessed permanency from promises. Explain accessible child influence without inferred consent; necessary sharing and accountable case-information practice; operational safeguarding beyond posters and counts; association, self-report, outcome and transfer limits in parenting evidence; and qualified coordinated emergency decisions. Require contextual evidence, competent responsibilities, feedback, supervision and review. Reading alone confers no badge or certificate: verified course passes, a configured mixed ParaLearn exam, criterion-level human marking, independent moderation, completion and authorised signatures remain required.
